$comment: Theme registry for ArchPatternsForAgents. Consumed by the ui-craft skill and by any project that asks this repo for a layout. Append themes and components over time; do not restructure without updating .github/skills/ui-craft/SKILL.md.

consume.how: Pick one theme id. Apply its tokens and technique. Author markup from the ui-craft element rules, NOT by copying a component whose conformance is visual-reference.

conformance_levels.conformant: Markup and operability pass the checker, and every control announces its purpose. Safe to copy structure and style.
conformance_levels.visual-reference: Aesthetic direction is correct; markup or operability does not pass. Copy the look, not the DOM.

consume.pick_a_look: Every theme ships a full page and a rendered image. Open themes/GALLERY.md, choose by eye, then read that theme's page.html for the finish and themes/_shared/substrate-contract.md for the rules it obeys.
consume.genre: Each theme declares a genre, a premise, the elements it leads with, and the elements it must refuse. Genre decides which data the surface shows at all; composition and finish follow from it. Two themes with the same genre are the same theme in two colours.
consume.controls: Asking for a control by kind? Read controls.kinds -- never copy the DOM of a visual-reference component; follow its use_instead.

themes.name: Gritty Cyberpunk
themes.world: A decker's rig in a neon-soaked dystopia. High contrast, slightly degraded, hyper-responsive.
themes.use_when: High-stakes or destructive actions, live system state, anything where the operator should feel the weight of a decision.
technique: layered box-shadow insets for extruded polymer and metal ledges
drop-shadow and text-shadow bloom on activation

defects: input is display:none — the control is unreachable by Tab and absent from the accessibility tree
glitch keyframes with no prefers-reduced-motion branch
83% div/span; the [ STATUS: SAFE ] readouts are a definition list rendered as divs
bracket glyphs are text content rather than ::before/::after
content:"" set on .switch-handle, a real element, where it is a no-op

components.note: Same visuals as override-toggle.html on a real substrate. Clipped checkbox rather than display:none; :checked, :focus-visible and :disabled drive every themed state; visual layer is aria-hidden so the accessible name comes from clipped label text; <output> announces state as a live region; prefers-reduced-motion guards the glitch and the spring travel. Telemetry is <dl>/<output>/<code>/<time>, brackets are ::before/::after.

themes.premise: An operator is about to do something irreversible and must feel the weight before committing.
themes.forbidden_note: No metrics grid and no estate table. This surface is about an act, not a status.

themes.name: Pristine Hyper-Minimalism
themes.world: A private orbital command deck. Stark, flawless, focused on spatial depth and fluid motion.
themes.use_when: Headline metrics, telemetry summaries, any surface whose job is one number read at a glance.
themes.ground: slow fluid mesh of four analogous oklch radial gradients over #050510
themes.type: geometric sans; massive thin display numeral against tiny tracked uppercase label
technique: 1px white border at 10% opacity plus inner top-edge highlight
no hard borders inside the pane
pointer-tracked rotateX/rotateY with cubic-bezier spring return

defects: 3D tilt transform with no prefers-reduced-motion branch
86% div/span; a metric with a label is <dl> or <output>, and any timestamp is <time datetime>
6 custom properties; a named palette wants 7-11

themes.premise: One number, read at a glance, from across a room. Everything else is subtraction.
themes.forbidden_note: The strictest list in the registry, and the point of the theme. A page whose job is one number does not need a table, a form group or a gauge.

themes.name: Deep Lab Tech
themes.world: An underground R&D facility. Utilitarian, data-dense, highly structured.
themes.use_when: Dense readouts, live signals, comparison matrices, anything an operator scans rather than reads.
themes.ground: very dark charcoal with a fine millimetre-paper SVG grid
themes.type: monospace throughout, tabular-lining numerals, hard alignment
technique: corner brackets via ::before/::after instead of continuous boxes
inline SVG waveform with feGaussianBlur phosphor bloom

defects: 95% div/span from a vocabulary of exactly div, span, svg — the worst substrate of the three generated themes, in the theme whose entire premise is dense scientific data
a frequency matrix is <table> with <caption> and <th scope>; a bounded reading is <meter>; a sample instant is <time datetime>
waveform animation with no prefers-reduced-motion branch
1 grid-template, so the advertised bento layout is one repeated shape
flat ground despite the theme calling for a millimetre-paper grid

themes.premise: An operator scans a comparison matrix looking for the outlier. Density is the feature.
themes.forbidden_note: None. A comparison matrix is genuinely a table; this is the one theme where it leads.

themes.name: The Nocturnal Forge
themes.world: A late-night workshop bridging compute, hardware and physical space.
themes.use_when: Home lab telemetry, machine control, long dark-room sessions.
technique: feTurbulence noise overlay for powder-coated metal
complex inset+outset box-shadow arrays to carve controls out of the ground
drag interaction with resistance, never free-spinning

defects: the dial is div drag handlers with no native control — no keyboard, no value, no role; it must be <input type=range> under the skin
91% div/span from a vocabulary of div, span, svg
a VRAM figure with a ceiling is <meter>, and its readout is <output>
flat ground despite the theme calling for a noise-textured surface

themes.premise: An operator adjusts a machine in a dark room and needs to feel the control move.
themes.forbidden_note: No estate table. A control panel that lists rows of data is a dashboard wearing a dial.

controls.note: Ask for a control by kind, not by theme. Each entry names the semantic substrate (fixed, never negotiable) and points at a conformant instance you can read in a working page. Copy the element and its state bindings; restyle the finish freely.
controls.resolve: themes/<page>#<element-id>. Open the page, find the id, take the element plus the CSS rules that key off :checked / :focus-visible / :disabled.

instances.finish: heavy mechanical throw switch, travels 80px, ignites on arm
tungsten latch, seats with an inset shadow
compact bracketed arm, four in a rack
standalone worked example, the one conformant component

kinds.proves: clipped with position/clip-path, never display:none, so Tab and Space still reach it

instances.finish: rotary, conic-gradient track burning orange, feTurbulence powder coat

kinds.proves: a rotary dial is a range input rotated by CSS; arrow keys move it and it announces a value
kinds.instead_of: nocturnal-forge/allocation-dial.html -- drag handlers, no form control, no keyboard, no value

instances.finish: vertical channel fader with a machined cap
flat phosphor slider, tabular readout beside it

kinds.proves: same substrate as the dial; only the finish differs
grouping is a fieldset, not a heading above buttons; arrow keys move within the group

instances.finish: cold metal until both interlocks satisfy

kinds.proves: the native disabled attribute holds the gate, so the paint cannot disagree with the state

instances.finish: terminal field, required text shown in code

kinds.proves: second interlock on an irreversible act

instances.finish: minimal, sits under the hero number

kinds.proves: native select keeps keyboard and platform picker behaviour

instances.finish: digital value in the dial face

kinds.proves: output is a live region by default, so a value change is announced
kinds.hazard: output is itself labelable. A <label> wrapping an output before an input binds to the output and leaves the input unnamed. Use explicit label[for].

kinds.proves: not a div with a width percentage
kinds.note: forbidden on gritty-cyberpunk and pristine-minimalism -- see each theme's forbidden list

instances.finish: 5-column estate matrix, corner brackets, no cell borders

kinds.proves: row and column relationships reach a screen reader
kinds.note: forbidden on the other three themes. A table is a genre decision, not a default.
